sentences.text: Writ Petition No. 6722 Of 2012

Mochi Samaj Sudhar Mandal, .. Petitioner
 Through its Secretary..
 Versus
 The State of Maharashtra & Ors. .. Respondents
Ms. Pradnya Talekar h/f. Talekar & Associates, Advocate for the petitioner.

Ms. R.P. Gour, Agp for respondent Nos. 1 to 6.
 Mr. Anand P. Bhandari, Advocate for respondent No.7.

Coram : Kishore C. Sant &
 Sushil M. Ghodeswar, Jj.
Reserved On : 17.02.2026 Pronounced On : 07.03.2026 Order

[PER : KISHOR C.
SANT,J.] : -
01.

By way of this petition, the petitioner - a registered trust has approached this Court for grant of 5 acres land for the purpose of rehabilitation of the members of the petitioner-trust, including the land in Gat No.19, situated at Kanchanwadi, Tal. &
Dist. Aurangabad.
It is further prayed that the petitioner trust be allotted 21 Gunthas land in land Survey No.3 in CTS No. 18235/1 situated at Padampura, Aurangabad for partial rehabilitation of the members.

Further 5 acres (2) wp6722.12 land be granted for rehabilitation of the members of the trust in Gat No. 29 at Kanchanwadi, Tal. &
Dist. Aurangabad.
02. Respondent Nos.1 to 6 are the State of Maharashtra and its Authorities.
Respondent No.7 is the Municipal Corporation, Aurangabad, through its Commissioner.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The petitioner is a public trust registered under the then Bombay Public Trusts Act.
The Registration Certificate is dated 08.08.1977.
It is averred in the petition that there are about 500 members of the trust belonging to Cobbler community, a caste recognized at Scheduled Caste.
The society had preferred various representations for allotment of land.
It is further stated that in 1958 the Government acquired land by passing award on 17.07.1958.
The land acquired is of 3 acres and 10 gunthas for re-settlement of persons belonging to Cobbler community.

It is case that, however,
the land actually is given to the Social Welfare Officer, Aurangabad on 19.05.1959 instead of members of the trust.
It is alleged that the said land thus was never used for the purpose of rehabilitation/ resettlement of the members of the trust.

Subsequently, the Corporation - respondent No.7 passed resolution to acquire land from CTS No. 18235/1, belonging to (3)
wp6722.12 one Harshwardhan Gautamchand Jain, which is the land acquired.
Later- on a hostel is constructed on plot bearing CTS No. 18235/1, namely Sant Tukaram Hostel.
In 2012, the petitioner sought information as to how the hostel is constructed on the land which was acquired for rehabilitation of the members of the trust and thus this petition is filed.
04. Learned Advocate Ms. Talekar for the petitioner vehemently argued that the total land of 3 acres 19 gunthas was acquired.
Possession of the same was taken in 1958.
When the land was acquired, it was acquired for the purpose of rehabilitation of the persons belonging to Cobbler community.
However, in 1980, said land is allotted for some other purpose.
Later-on, the Corporation in its meeting dated 11.07.2001 passed a resolution wherein it is shown that the land is acquired for construction of the school.
However, the land is given to one Jagjivanram Magasvargiya Gruhnirman Sanstha and there are disputes.

The land bearing No. 18325/1, admeasuring 910.9 sq.
ft. is open land that sought to be acquired.
Even amount towards compensation of the said land was deposited.
The said land was standing in the name of Kashinath Navandar and Vajrachand Jain.
She further submits that one sale-deed is also executed.
The land was purchased by Aurangabad Municipal Corporation in 2002 for Rs. 25,96,064/- on 09.09.2002 and a hostel is (4) wp6722.12 constructed.
It was never reserved for the said purpose.
She submits that different stands are adopted from time to time.
Though there is another land acquired in 1968, however, same is also allotted for the different purpose and as on today no land is allotted for rehabilitation of the members of the trust.
She therefore submits that the petition deserves to be allowed.
05. Learned AGP opposes this petition.

She submits that the petitioner trust is registered in 1977,
therefore, there is no question of the said trust being in existence in 1958.

Her submission,
therefore, that the land was acquired in 1958 for the members of the trust cannot be accepted.
There is no list of members provided along with the petition.
Action done in 1958 is sought to be challenged by filing present petition in 2012.
There is no resolution of the trust on record for filing this petition.
There is no representation made by the petitioner to any Authority.
The land is already given to Jagjivanram Co-operative Housing Society and that is an accepted position.

In view of this,
it cannot be said that the land is not used for the purpose for which it is acquired.
Land Survey No.3 registered in the name of Social Welfare Department is in the possession of the Jagjivanram Co-operative Housing Society.
She thus submits that the petitioner-trust has failed to show any right vested (5) wp6722.12 in it.
Learned AGP thus submits that the petition deserves to be dismissed with heavy costs.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Learned Advocate Mr. Bhandari for respondent No.7- Corporation submits that there is registered sale-deed in their favour.
There is no challenge to the said sale-deed.
The question is only about 3 acres and 10 gunthas land.
Now, only 9 gunthas land is left and same is also sold to the Corporation.
He thus submits that as on today, there is no land available.
He also prays for dismissal of the petition.
07. In rebuttal, learned Advocate for the petitioner submits that Jagjivanram Co-operative Housing Society is a housing society.
Unless the petitioner is allotted the land, the purpose of acquisition would not be fulfilled.
08. This Court has gone through the petition paper book.
It is seen that one Jagjivanram Co-operative Housing Society had also filed writ petition in 2015 for the relief of declaration that the resolution for reservation of land for school is lapsed.
Said petition was allowed.
It is also seen that even a contempt petition was filed.

Writ petition No. 1692 of 2004 was filed by Mainabai Pardeshi and Bhaulal Gumaldu along with (6) wp6722.12 other petitions, wherein this Court has again allowed the petition declaring that the proceeding has lapsed.
Therefore, the acquisition was directed, if required.
Writ Petition No. 5596 of 2007 came to be dismissed.

This petition was filed by Jagjivanram Co-operative Housing Society praying for directions to the Government to make funds available for acquisition of land Survey No.12 admeasuring 52 R, which came to be dismissed.
09. By considering the arguments of both the sides and the documents on record, it is clearly seen that the petitioner-trust itself is registered in 1977.
There was no question of acquiring land for their purpose in the year 1958 and 1968.
The land acquired is already put to use, wherein a hostel is constructed for the students belonging to the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes.
This Court does not find any merit in the writ petition.
This Writ Petition, therefore, deserves to be dismissed and the same is dismissed with no order as to costs.

[SUSHIL M. GHODESWAR, J.] [KISHORE C. SANT, J.]
